why: The function sits in the top few singular directions, so base + rank-8 recovers about 80% of the plain T 1.0 gain (base ~45, RL ~93 on these 100), as the theory's own 435/500 prediction implies at T 0.6.
Rank-8 truncation carries the coherent low-rank part, so it should recover about 80% of the 224 -> 463 plain T 1.0 gain rather than its 11.8% energy share.
A random rank-8 update of the same small norm has none of the deliberation/format directions, so it stays at plain base level (~45 of 100).
Removing the top-8 directions leaves base plus the high-rank optimizer noise, which does almost nothing, so accuracy falls most of the way back toward plain base.
The delta minus its top-64 directions is pure high-rank remainder holding most of the energy but little function, so it scores close to plain base.
One coherent direction per matrix already carries a large part of the low-rank readout, so rank-1 recovers about half the gain (theory's 390/500 at T 0.6 scaled to plain T 1.0).
The functional low-rank part is spread over all matrices, so just 24 late-MLP terms carry only a small share and leave the model mostly base-like.
Recovery comes along the single format/length readout, so the rank-8 arm takes RL's long boxed deliberation style (RL plain 4,694 tokens, theta 0.5 plain 4,536).
